disagreements.their_reason: A fitted artifact other than basis, coordinates, or head weights changing on append would falsify 'no fitted artifact'; only those three are fingerprinted.
Same-run fitted-artifact fingerprints changing would falsify the attribution to store-only learning; fingerprints come only from a separate experiment.
A paired comparison differing only in downstream edges could show no breakage reduction; differing edit and ambiguity counts mean this evidence does not isolate that intervention.
A matched-question zero-shot versus trained comparison with a gap above 0.15 would falsify it; the reported groups differ sharply in size and definition.
A representation winning both generalisation and precision would falsify the tradeoff, but the scope retreats to three post-hoc, cross-corpus experiments that never measure both axes together.
A persistent positive gap beyond 10 aliases would falsify the claim that alias supply explains the disadvantage; a shrinking but still nonzero curve does not rule that out.

0.reason: A fitted artifact other than basis, coordinates, or head weights changing on append would falsify 'no fitted artifact'; only those three are fingerprinted.

1.reason: Entity penalty exceeding relation penalty at depth 1, or depth-2 penalty below 0.10, would falsify it; the scoped measurements rule both out.

2.reason: Same-run fitted-artifact fingerprints changing would falsify the attribution to store-only learning; fingerprints come only from a separate experiment.

3.reason: Old-answer persistence exceeding refusal or other wrong answers would falsify it; 1 stale case versus 150 refusals and 82 other answers rules that out.

4.reason: A paired comparison differing only in downstream edges could show no breakage reduction; differing edit and ambiguity counts mean this evidence does not isolate that intervention.

5.reason: A depth-2 held-out/trained gap above 0.02 at 61 relations would falsify it; the measured gap is 0.011.

6.reason: Failure of the specified walker to beat the same-question planner would falsify the stated result; 0.912 versus 0.534 rules it out within the narrow formulation.

7.reason: A matched-question zero-shot versus trained comparison with a gap above 0.15 would falsify it; the reported groups differ sharply in size and definition.

8.reason: Refusal materially below 0.970 on the scoped sparse chain-break population would falsify it; 5821 of 6000 rules that out.

9.reason: Failure to raise not-applicable refusal or reduce answerable wrongness would falsify it; both scoped before/after measurements move as claimed.

10.reason: Nonnegative or absent within-population branching/refusal correlations would falsify it; all three measured correlations are strongly negative.

11.reason: A representation winning both generalisation and precision would falsify the tradeoff, but the scope retreats to three post-hoc, cross-corpus experiments that never measure both axes together.

12.reason: A persistent positive gap beyond 10 aliases would falsify the claim that alias supply explains the disadvantage; a shrinking but still nonzero curve does not rule that out.

13.reason: A head gap above 0.05 in any scoped population would falsify 'free'; all three within-corpus gaps remain below that threshold while retrieval drops substantially.
